previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of type 2 diabetes, kidney transplant, and peripheral artery disease was admitted for evaluation of shaking chills following a punch biopsy of a chronic left lower leg ulcer. The biopsy confirmed calciphylaxis, explaining his symptoms. Blood and urine cultures were negative, and antibiotics were discontinued after four days. He underwent successful placement of a port for administration of intravenous sodium thiosulfate, which was initiated during the admission. Cinacalcet was started and vitamin D stopped to manage calcium metabolism. His acute kidney injury resolved with hydration, and his blood pressure was controlled on home medications. He was discharged home with plans for outpatient sodium thiosulfate infusions, wound care, and follow-up with dermatology and transplant nephrology.

ACTIVE PROBLEMS:
================
# R hand pain: The etiology is most likely secondary to 
microvascular disease. Less likely secondary to calciphylaxis. 
The patient has significant peripheral vascular disease and 
multiple amputations, and the digits were cool to touch. 
Vascular surgery ordered a RUE Doppler study, which was 
equivocal; they suggested a RUE angiogram should further 
evaluation of the finger wound be needed. However, as this was 
felt to be largely due to microvascular disease, further imaging 
felt not to provide benefit; Vascular recommended symptomatic 
therapy with pain control, and outpatient follow up. The lesion 
was felt unlikely to be an embolic phenomenon, as TEE without 
evidence of endocarditis. The patient's pain was managed with 
oxycontin 20mg PO qAM, 30mg PO qPM. He was also given oxycodone 
5mg for breakthrough pain. In addition he was started on 
gabapentin 300mg PO TID, which may be uptitrated as an 
outpatient. On discharge, his right finger/hand pain was ___, 
and he was able to carry out activities of daily living with 
this pain level. 

# Calciphylaxis
# Lower left leg ulcer
# Necrotizing Fasciitis: Pathology consistent with 
calciphylaxis. Per last admission, the patient was started on 
STS IV to finish as an outpatient. Recent port placement on 
___. However, wound appeared to be larger that prior admission 
and patient in great deal of pain. Vascular surgery involved and 
debrided the area, and appearance/microbiology of the underlying 
wound was consistent with necrotizing fasciitis. A wound vac was 
placed over the debrided area and changed every 3 days. The 
patient was treated with zosyn, which should be continued until 
___. Dermatology also followed the patient. He continued his 
IV sodium thiosulfate at 25mg three times weekly. He tolerated 
the STS well although with minor increase in his anion gap. 
Cinacalet was discontinued during the admission. Dermatology 
also wanted to check RPR given his involvement of hands and 
soles, and this was negative. The pain service followed the 
patient given his extensive pain. The patient was discharged on 
the following medications: tylenol ___ Q8H, oxyconTIN 20mg 
qAM and 30mg qPM, ___ oxycodone Q4H:PRN breakthrough pain, 
and gabapentin 300mg TID. The patient denied leg pain on 
discharge. The patient will have outpatient follow up with 
plastic surgery to close his left leg wound. He will also have 
outpatient follow up with Dermatology. 

# ___: The patient's admission creatinine was 1.9, with baseline 
of 1.5. Likely pre-renal etiology given poor PO intake, recent 
diarrhea, and fluid-responsiveness. ___ initially improved to 
baseline, however, the patient underwent contrast study 
(arteriogram) on ___, after which he experienced elevated 
creatinine to peak of 2.2, which trended down. Discharge 
creatinine was 1.8.

# Hypertension
The patient's hypertension was asymptomatic, but very difficult 
to control. He often had systolic blood pressures above 200 
despite maximum doses of antihypertensive medications. Labetalol 
was up titrated to 800 mg 3 times daily. During the admission 
the patient was placed on hydralazine, however due to concern of 
tachyphylaxis, this medication was discontinued. Doxazosin was 
discontinued, and clonidine 0.1 mcg patch was started. In 
addition Chlorthalidone 25 mg p.o. daily was started. In 
addition, minoxidil 10mg PO daily was started. We continued 
aspirin and nifedipine ER 60mg BID. Initially spironolactone was 
held in the setting of acute kidney injury, but this was 
restarted once kidney function recovered. It is possible pain 
secondary to poor vascularization of digits played a role in the 
patient's hypertension.

#Suspicion for endocarditis:
Patient with questionable vegetations on aortic valve on his TTE 
___. There was concern for endocarditis and embolic phenomena 
which his third finger wound and leukocytoclastic vasculitis. 
Therefore, the patient was placed on vancomycin and cefepime. 
Blood cultures were negative. TEE showed no vegetations, so 
vancomycin was discontinued.

# Diarrhea: 
The patient initially reported that he was having low grade 
fevers, malaise, and diarrhea upon admission. However, diarrhea 
quickly resolved. C.diff was negative. His urine culture was 
negative and blood cultures were negative.
